q: On a Words in Context question, what do you do before looking at the answer choices?
choices: Say your own word for the blank using clues in the sentence

q: The passage says the plants survived three frosts "with little damage." Why is "indestructible" wrong?
choices: It is too extreme: little damage is still some damage
It is the opposite of the passage
It is a near miss in grammar

q: On a Central Ideas question, a choice is about one detail, not the whole passage. What is wrong with it?
choices: Nothing, details are always the main idea
